summary.intent: Continue driving the CipherBox v2 engine write-plane wayfinder map (#813) through successive HITL grilling tickets to resolve open design forks, then implement, ship, and merge the resulting backlog issues while the user was AFK.
summary.outcome: Resolved wayfinder tickets #814, #815, #816(research), #817, #818, #819, #821, #823, and #822 (with three new sub-questions filed), shipped four backlog issues (#827, #833, #798, #794) through the full /ship loop with PRs #835/#834/#838 merged and #839 rebased and ready, and filed several new issues (#830, #831, #832, #836, #837, plus quota-ambiguity tickets) capturing residual gaps.

repo: The engine currently has NO production write/publish path at all — seal_content, dag::assemble, sync/tick.rs::run_tick_loop, and ApiClient::upload/quota have zero non-test callers; a plain mkdir stages an op that publishes nothing, ever

register-first is about keeping a live IPNS name from ever being uninventoried, not about content CIDs; NameRegistration has no CID-only form, so pre-registering CIDs mints a null-head name-inventory row the republisher iterates

Re-uploading is free: registerPin short-circuits an already-pinned CID at size>0 with no new charge, and since content is sealed once at command time and staged, retries regenerate byte-identical CIDs — so rollback/retire only fires on abandonment, never on transient failure

The adoption gate's floor law is single-writer: gate/floor.rs is the only place sequence/epoch floors advance, and only via AAD-confirmed unseal (stage 6) — a write path must never pre-raise the floor itself or its own record permanently fails to cache
StagingStore (op queue + staged bytes) is ONE seam on ONE origin bucket (IndexedDB+OPFS on web) — 'key rides the op' vs 'key beside the bytes' is not two options, it's one security decision
put_staged_bytes replaces rather than appends, forcing per-block staging keys (not one blob) once multi-block writes were chosen, which in turn forces orphan_staging_keys/stage_op rework

enc-subkey derives from loginSecret (identity-level, epoch-independent) while read_key derives through the scope seed (epoch-dependent, no epoch→seed map kept client-side) — the wrong anchor for sealing a queued content key would break across rotations

content blocks are self-verifying by CID (verify_cid) and served accelerator-first (our own Kubo, the node the upload just pinned to) — so a sealed-block read cache is pure latency/perf, never a correctness requirement

users.byo is a two-state flag but PinMode is three-state; the API 409s hosted ingress for byo=true accounts, so PinMode should be a purely client-side policy (byo ⇔ External) rather than a server-known mode, avoiding a costly live-trust-gate migration

'sealed in vault settings' (per engine.md/api.md) has no v2 home — ReadBody has only Folder/File variants; it's a v1 IPNS-record carryover with no current implementation, so BYO provider config needs a new sealed API blob instead
Confirm-by-re-resolve in net/publish.rs collapses 'network unreadable' and 'record not there' into the same None → Published outcome, silently masking the exact residual #817 accepted as a known gap

ChildRef has no version/sequence field, which determines which ops publish one record vs two, and 'a reference must never outlive its referent' is the single ordering law governing all multi-publish ops (create, delete, relink)

CodeRabbit and Greptile share review duty but Greptile is credit-paused org-wide until 2026-08-18, and CodeRabbit's web review + CLI pass share one org-wide rate limit (~1/hr), making a 4-PR batch a ~4-hour pipeline regardless of implementation speed

code.finding: stage_op fails closed on a content op with a staging key but no upload bytes; the budget is checked and bytes staged BEFORE the op is enqueued, establishing seal-at-command as already contractually bound, not a live choice

snapshot_cache.put only fires on the Adopted arm; SequenceNotNewer{sequence==floor} routes to Current, which never writes the cache — so a write path that pre-raises the floor leaves its own record permanently uncached

fanout_get_verify's None result (endpoint error, no record, or unverifiable garbage all collapse together) falls through to PublishOutcome::Published — the exact mechanism behind the accepted 'published but never resolvable' residual
HeldRecord deliberately stores only the narrow per-name Ed25519 signer, not the scope write seed, per least-privilege rules 2/5 — this is the decisive precedent against a custody-bearing publish port

register() inserts pin rows at size:'0' with no Kubo call and no quota gate; name rows are {accountId, ipnsName, headCid: head ?? null} — pre-registering CIDs mints a null-head name-inventory row the republisher iterates

Hosted ingress is hard-refused for byo=true accounts under a pessimistic_write row lock (ConflictException), and registerPin idempotently short-circuits an already-pinned CID (size>0) with no new charge, promoting size:'0' registry-only rows

Original code discarded SyncAccessHandle.write()'s bytesWritten return value and never called persist(); fixed (commit 07b54ae01) to catch both short-write and thrown-error paths into one failure value with unconditional cleanup

owner_root_fixture sealed the owner-write-blob under a fixed EPH_OWNER_WRITE ephemeral with a fixed owner_enc across differing owner_write_blob_epoch values, reusing an HPKE keystream across epochs — flagged Major by CodeRabbit and fixed by varying enc_scalar per epoch (commit 1c9142dec)

workflow: Wayfinder skill: charting mode names destination via grilling then stops (never resolves tickets); work-through-the-map mode claims one ticket, resolves via AskUserQuestion with pros/cons, records resolution as a GitHub comment, closes, updates map — caps at one resolved ticket per session except research tickets, unless the user explicitly directs successive tickets

User has repeatedly (5+ times across the whole engagement) rejected AskUserQuestion prompts that lead with mechanism/recommendation instead of explicit per-option pros/cons grounded in file:line facts — this is the dominant recurring feedback signal

Sibling background agents sharing one git checkout can clobber each other's branch refs (one ends up empty) when both do checkout -b + commit concurrently; fix is git branch -f <branch> <sha>, and a safer pattern is an isolated git worktree off main per agent

Delegating 'wait ~1hr for a rate limit then act' to a background agent is unreliable — the harness's 600s stream-idle watchdog kills agents that produce no output while blocked on an external cooldown; fix is to run the wait as a directly-owned background shell command/Monitor and only spawn agents when there's immediate work
CodeRabbit findings can land in the review body ('Actionable comments posted: N') rather than as inline review threads — querying reviewThreads alone can wrongly conclude a PR is clean
gh pr edit is broken on this repo; PR bodies must be patched via gh api -X PATCH .../pulls/<N> -F body=@file

/ship is the full canonical loop (verify, security-review, conditional crypto-privacy-review, simplify, local gate suites, CodeRabbit CLI, draft PR, resolve-pr-reviews) — hand-rolling a subset of it (as was initially done briefing 4 workers) omits real steps
